Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary v Outlook for 2008:
Consumption and Production to Increase by 2.2% and 3.1%
- World consumption is estimated to grow by 2.2% to reach 14.6Mt
- Credit crunch depressed consumption in developed countries by -2.1%
- Consumption in developing markets is growing at 5.9%
- World production is expected to rise by 3.1%
- Developing countries are the main drivers of this year’s output growth, rising
by 8.2% this year; developed country production will fall by 2.3%
- Trade surplus in Western Europe will grow by 90% from 2007 while that of
North East Asia will deteriorate; Trade deficit of North America is expected
to deteriorate by 34% to 87,000 tonnes
- World capacity is expected to increase by 6.5% this year, main gainers are
China, the Middle East and Eastern and Central Europe
- Global capacity utilisation will decline from 70% in 2007 to 68% in 2008
Near Term Outlook for 2009:
Capacity Will Continue to Grow Faster than Production
- World consumption

to grow by 3.5%, led by developing countries
- China will not rebound quickly from 2008 due to tight monetary policies
- Western Europe will see largest fall in consumption
- World production growth of 3.5% in 2009
- Wirerod net exports of developed countries to shrink by 96kt to 179kt
- Taiwan and Korea will see decline in net exports of 74kt to 157kt
- Capacity to grow by 6.6%, driven by China and the Middle East
- Global capacity utilisation rates to decline to 66%
Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary vi Forecast for the Period 2010-2012:
Global Capacity Utilisation to Recover by 2012
- World consumption is expected to grow by 5.3% on CAGR basis
- Developed markets will grow by only 0.3% while developing markets will
grow by 8.7%
- World production is forecast to rise by 5.3% without taking into account
stock changes
- There will be a further narrowing of developed country net export position
with the developing markets
- Capacity growth is forecast to rise by 11% with China being the main driver
- We anticipate the closure of Nexans’ Canadian mill
- Global capacity utilisation will recover to 69% by 2012 with developed
country utilisation at 71% and developing at 68%

Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary Implications for copper wirerod industry 2008-2012 (1)
- The current world economic slowdown will accelerate globalisation. Cost
cutting was the reaction in 2001/02; so it is again now – customers migrate.
- Recessionary cycles – will be deeper and longer in industrialised markets.
Construction cable markets are not going to “bounce back” any time soon.
- All of the growth in world wirerod production (+51%) will occur in developing
regions; Industrialised regions will see volumes decline by -5%.
- Similarly, all world wirerod consumption growth (+45%) will occur in
developing regions; Industrialised regions will see volumes fall by 3%.
- “Last man standing” is a viable business strategy in

a declining regional
market. Russian rod imports are the main threat to exits by other mills.
- Russian rod traders will be opportunistic, spoiling and quick to exploit local
rod shortages. Main counter is quality, flexibility and reliable deliveries.
- Chinese/Russian rod production volumes will grow faster than expected; rod
quality will probably also improve faster with new technology and experience.
Implications for copper wirerod industry 2008-2012 (cont.)
- High energy and transport costs will be unrelenting. Although expensive,
relocation of existing capacity closer to consumers should be considered.
- Also, early retirement of older less efficient mills in inferior/outdated locations.
- Replacement by fewer but newer large scale energy efficient mills close to
the new location of the low cost wire and cable customer base.
- Rod mills can anticipate cable industry migration to lower cost centres, and
site new capacity accordingly, actively pulling customers towards them.
- New capacity in industrialising economies will increasingly be sited at
copper refineries or at accessible port / transport hub locations.
- Developing Asia, Middle East – North Africa (MENA) and Eastern & Central
Europe have become the new arteries of production / consumption growth.
- Direct involvement in one or more of these regions will guarantee growth.
Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary ix Implications for copper cathode sellers 2008-2012
- Continuing expansion in Developing Asia and Eastern and Central Europe,
but Middle East – North Africa (MENA) will be the main new axis of growth.
- New rod projects in MENA will be desperate to secure cathode supplies.
- China will revive when copper prices fall and when tighter domestic monetary
policy is relaxed. But growth rates will not rebound, ranging from 9-13% p.a.
- The structure of Chinese rod production is changing rapidly in favour of local
vertically integrated copper companies who are investing in the next
generation of large scale, energy efficient, rod mills sited at refineries…
- …as a result, the mass of small scale inefficient poor quality mills operating
Chinese Upcast technology will be starved of domestic cathode.
- China, the Gulf States, Turkey, India, Russia, Egypt, Eastern Europe, Iran,
Indonesia, Vietnam and North Africa will outperform industrialised markets.
Implications for the wire & cable industry 2008-2012
- Is operating a rod mill for internal use, or for open market sale, still a core
part of our business model? What are the working capital implications?
- The closure or reduction of regional rod capacity does have implications for
the continued viability of existing w

ire and cable plant locations.
- The opening or expansion of regional rod capacity should influence plans for
the location of new wire and cable plants, and expansions.
- High copper prices, wirerod industry mergers, withdrawals from open market
supply, will restrict options for future rod supply and premia negotiations
- Wire & cable companies and OEM customers are relocating but the rod
industry needs to follow to guarantee reliable, quality supply at good prices…
- …surely there is an opportunity here for closer supply chain partnerships!
Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary x Implications for wirerod equipment suppliers 2008-2012
- The appetite for new large scale energy efficient mills in Developing Asia,
MENA and Eastern & Central Europe will be undiminished.
- There will also be continuing opportunities for small scale casting units.
- China, the Gulf States, Turkey, India, Russia, Egypt, Eastern Europe, Iran,
Indonesia, Vietnam and, eventually, North Africa will be the hot spots.
- Integrated copper refinery customers offer the best potential for firm orders.
- Equipment suppliers should work harder with new mill project owners to
secure cathode feedstock in advance, to avoid commissioning delays.
- Further research and development on scrap consuming systems is likely to
pay dividends in the future (scrap supply may be easier than for cathode).
- Further research and development into energy efficient casting technology
systems will also dovetail with consumers needs in a high energy cost world.

Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary xiii Conclusions 1): World Copper Wirerod Consumption
- World demand grew from 11.3mt to 14.3mt in 2000-07 at a CAGR of +3.4%
- The trend is cyclical, but with erratic year to year variations, due to stock +/-
- 2004 (+8.6%) and 2007 (+5.8%) were the peaks in the current cycle…
- …inevitably followed by troughs in 2005 (+1.3%) and 2008 (+2.2% forecast)
- Wirerod consumption is a “derived demand” from copper cable output
- Economic factors determine world copper cable demand and output but…
- …Globalisation now dictates where this growth occurs (and where it does not)
- Developing Asia, E&C Europe, RoW all grew at CAGR of +10% (2000-07)
- Demand in all industrialised regions fell at a CAGR of -1% (2000-07)
- Developing regions: 51% of world offtake in 2007 (up from 33% in 2000) …
- …their demand is now growing at the expense of industrialised regions

Copper Semis Service – Copper Wirerod - Executive Summary xviii Conclusions 2): Regional Copper Wirerod Production
- N. America is in decline as a rod producer. Weak US$ has deflected imports
but consumption is declining and Russian imports will inevitably return.
- W. European output is in relative decline; world share has fallen from 22% to
18%. Last UK mill shut in 2006, France in voluntary decline, but growth in
Spain, Italy, Belgium and Germany as mills capture market share.
- E&C Europe more than doubles output to 1.4mt. Supplying gro

wing regional
consumption, and international market through incentivised Russian exports.
- NE Asia in absolute decline as wirerod exports fall. Regional cable industry
output decreasing, undercut by cheaper offshore wire and cable imports.
- Developing Asia share surges from 19% to 34%. “4 main positives forces”:
local output replaces imports; demand surges from economic development;
inward migration of cable consumers / producers; rising wire & cable exports.
- RoW output growth constrained by capacity and cathode availability in 2007.
Set to change massively through 2008-2012 due to multitude of new projects.

Conclusions: Copper Wirerod & Drawn Wire Trade
- World trade grew from 2.61mt in 2000 to 3.35mt in 2007 at a CAGR of +3.6%
- 83% of trade is in wirerod, 11% in single strand wire and 6% in stranded wire
- Russia (516kt), Germany (487kt) and France (253kt) are the top exporters
- China (346kt), Middle East (306kt) and the USA (249kt) are the top importers
- Chinese net imports peaked at 499kt in 2004, and are now in decline…
- …this has hit wirerod and wire exports from Korea, Taiwan and Japan
- Russian net exports were 513kt in 2007 (including one-off sales from stock)
- Rising net imports in the Middle East, North Africa & Eastern Europe
- Weak US dollar defends American rod mills from Russia, Brazil and Canada
- Germany, Russia, Egypt, India, Italy and Belgium are fast growing exporters
- Geographic proximity to consumers becoming the key competitive advantage
